text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: GPU pool saturation + autoscaler mismatch in us-west-2. Impacting /v1/generate for several customers. Severity: P1. Please ack and post initial triage.

Alex: Acked. I'm on it. Seeing elevated queue depth on infer-queue and HPA not scaling beyond 2 replicas.

Mira: I'm checking the HPA and cluster autoscaler metrics now. Linking dashboards: https://dash.redwood/cluster/us-west-2/autoscale and https://dash.redwood/serving/pool/gpu-pool-3

Devin: Customer-facing note: some requests are 5-20s slower, errors are 503s when queue overflow hits fallback. I'll prep a short message for support.

Alex: Quick live summary from my side: around 12:06 UTC we saw a spike in incoming tokens per second from a customer burst -> queue depth jumped from ~40 to ~620. GPU pods at 98% mem/util and 100% vram. HPA desiredReplicas stuck at 2 despite target metric (queue_depth) showing >500.

Priya: Hypothesis 1: HPA metric adapter (custom queue depth exporter) lagging -> HPA isn't seeing the spike so it won't scale. Hypothesis 2: Cluster autoscaler concedes because of pending warmup constraints (taints/affinity) -> nodes not provisioning fast enough. Hypothesis 3: Serving runtime warmup delay (model cold start) causing pods to be ready but not warm for inference, so they don't reduce queue quickly.

Alex: Sharing quick logs and commands I ran:

```
# hpa snapshot
kubectl get hpa -n serving infer-deployment-hpa -o yaml
metrics:
  current: 95% (queue_depth=620)
  desired: 2
  max: 10
```

```
# queue exporter sample (last 5m)
curl -s http://metrics.internal/queue/infer-queue | jq '.samples | .[-1]'
{"ts":"2026-03-15T12:07:02Z","queue_depth":618}
```

```
# node scale activity
kubectl get nodes --selector=pool=gpu-pool-3
NAME                                  STATUS   ROLES    AGE
g-01-abc                              Ready    <none>   12d
g-02-def                              Ready    <none>   6d
(autoscaler pending provisioning logs show requests queued for 4m)
```

Mira: I pulled the autoscaler logs — there's a rate-limiter backoff in the cloud provider API calls around 12:05-12:09 that caused node provisioning to stall. Log snippet:

```
2026-03-15T12:05:23Z autoscaler controller: requestNodeGroupSizeChange failed: 429 TooManyRequests -> retrying in 30s
2026-03-15T12:06:00Z autoscaler controller: provisioning delayed, outstandingRequests=3
```

Devin: So sequence seems to be: customer burst -> queue spike -> HPA metrics show high queue but HPA didn't request >2? Alex, you saw HPA desired stuck. Any reason HPA refused to scale (e.g., minReplicas config)?

Alex: HPA min=1 max=10. No misconfig. But I see the metric adapter returned the queue_depth as "gauge" not "avg over pods" for last minute, and HPA target was configured against avg queue per pod. The exporter reported the cluster-wide queue, so HPA calculus ended up with normalized value lower than threshold. I think metric mismatch is root cause for HPA not triggering enough replicas.

Priya: Adding to that: even if HPA had scaled fast, node provisioning stalled due to cloud rate limits -> warmup delay. So combined failure: metric mismatch + provisioning delays = saturation.

sre-ops-bot: Incident annotation: mitigation action 12:08 UTC -> manual scale to 6 replicas executed by Alex. 12:10 UTC -> cluster admin requested emergency node pool increase (hotfix). 12:14 UTC -> partial traffic reroute to fallback cluster in eu-west-1 for affected customers.

Alex: Manual scale command I ran:
```
kubectl scale deploy infer-deployment --replicas=6 -n serving
```
Response: new pods scheduling, but first warmup for model takes ~30-45s. Once warm, queue came down from 620 -> 80 over 2m.

Mira: Observed customer error spikes: 12:06-12:13 saw a 7.8% 5xx rate on /v1/generate for customers on us-west-2. Support note drafts in #support-daily.

Devin: Live mitigation checklist we did: 1) Manual scale to 6 2) Emergency node pool increase 3) Traffic split to eu fallback for top 3 customers 4) Short term model fallback to smaller quantized variant for batch jobs -> reduced per-request warmup.

Alex: For RCA coordination we should build a timeline and track evidence per hypothesis. I'll start a timeline below (rough times UTC):
- 12:04: incoming p95 traffic spike begins (customer A spawns parallel jobs)
- 12:05: queue depth climbs rapidly (>200)
- 12:06: autoscaler cloud API rate-limit kicks in (429), node provisioning delayed
- 12:06: HPA sees metrics but due to exporter mismatch computes desired=2 -> no scale
- 12:08: manual scale -> desired=6 applied
- 12:09-12:11: pods coming up, warmup delays (30-45s) -> continued high queue and some 503s
- 12:12: traffic reroute and node pool grows -> queue starts to fall
- 12:15: system stable, serving latency and error rates normalizing

Priya: Action items (assignments):
- fix metric exporter to expose avg queue per pod correctly (owner: Mira)
- add HPA test for gauge vs avg mismatch in CI (owner: Alex)
- engage cloud infra to understand/raise rate-limit windows or increase quota for autoscaler (owner: Taylor)
- explore warm pool / hot standby nodes for GPU pool to reduce cold-start (owner: Devin)
- customer postmortem and support messaging (owner: Devin + Priya)

Mira: I'm attaching the raw exporter snippet I found:
```
# queue_exporter.py: we emit total_queue_depth instead of avg_per_pod
metrics.gauge('infer_queue_total', total)
# should instead do:
metrics.gauge('infer_queue_per_pod_avg', total / max(1, ready_pods))
```

Alex: Quick experiment suggestion: change adapter to compute avg and watch HPA reaction in staging. Also consider HPA scale metrics smoothing window to avoid hiccups during spikes.

Devin: Customer comms: I'll send an interim note: "We experienced elevated latencies and retries in us-west-2 between 12:05–12:15 UTC due to capacity shortfall; traffic has been rerouted and we have scaled capacity. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with RCA."

sre-ops-bot: Handoff note: If this thread goes beyond shift change, please @oncall-next to pick up timeline. Next oncall is taylor (shift starts 12:30 UTC).

Taylor: I'll take post-incident actions after I'm on. For now adding a mitigation patch to increase autoscaler retry backoff jitter to avoid in-phase rate-limit storms.

Priya: One more note — metrics to attach to final RCA: queue depth timeseries, HPA events, autoscaler cloud API error rates, pod warmup latency histogram, per-customer token rates. We should snapshot dashboards now.

Alex: I've exported the relevant logs to the incident s3 bucket: s3://incidents/1795000123/logs.tar.gz (contains kube events, autoscaler logs, exporter logs).

Mira: I'm starting a draft RCA doc in drive: https://drive.redwood/incidents/1795000123-rca. I'll populate timeline + hypotheses and mark required evidence fields.

Devin: Closing loop on customer impact: 3 enterprise customers saw intermittent 503s, temporary SL degradation. Support notified.

Alex: If anyone finds more anomalies in autoscaler logs (like another 429 backoff cluster-wide) drop them here. Otherwise I'll start writing the RCA with the metric mismatch + cloud rate-limit combo as the primary cause.

Priya: Agreed. I'll create PRs for the exporter fix and a separate ops runbook for emergency node pool increases.

sre-ops-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 at 12:20 UTC after traffic reroute and scaling mitigations.

Mira: Final note: consider adding a fallback path in serving runtime to reject new long-running token-generation jobs when queue depth > threshold per customer to protect multi-tenant fairness.

Alex: Thanks everyone. Handing off to Taylor for follow-ups.

Taylor: Ack. Picking up next steps and will coordinate infra quota requests with cloud partner.

(reef of reactions: :thumbsup:, :eyes:, :rotating_light:)
